verdict.line: You lose if you walk into Boomerang Throw poke while Gnar's Hop is up and let him kite you at range; you win if you close the gap with E or stacked Q the moment his Hop is on cooldown and chain W into R before he hits max Rage.

brief.thesis: This matchup is a fight over distance: Gnar in Mini form is a ranged poker with no stun until Rage maxes him into Mega Gnar, while K'Sante has no gap closer besides a single early E point and no real all-in tool until R unlocks at 6. The 45.2% head-to-head over 2352 games is even because both sides are waiting on the same thing — Gnar waiting to land free Q pokes and escape with Hop, K'Sante waiting for Hop to be down so he can dash in. Solo-kill equity sits with K'Sante, so patience into a single clean engage wins the lane.

theirWindow.when: Hop is up, Gnar sitting at range
theirWindow.what: Don't walk forward to contest waves here — Q (Boomerang Throw) hits at 1100 range and slows, and he cuts its 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown further by catching it on the return. Let him have cheap minions rather than eat free pokes.

yourWindow.when: Hop down after a jump or juke
yourWindow.what: E (Footwork) dashes you in immediately, then stack Q (Ntofo Strikes) for the 2-stack shockwave pull or go straight to W (Path Maker)'s stun once he's out of escape options. This is the all-in window the solo-kill data favors you in.

start.why: Highest win rate and dominant pick (45.6% over 1802 games, 68.5% pick) — the bonus AD and sustain help you punish melee trades once you close distance rather than just surviving poke.

boots.why: 87.3% pick and the better of the two options (45%) — Gnar's damage in this lane leans on autos (basic Hyper-empowered attacks and Boomerang), so flat reduction on physical hits matters more than magic resist.

core.why: Gives you the AoE slow-on-hit that helps you actually stick to Gnar after an E (Footwork) engage instead of letting him Hop away again.
Converts your tank stats into damage and shielding for extended trades — part of the 49.6% win rate path over 131 games.
Stacking resistances closes out the build path with the highest measured win rate (49.6%) and lets you tank skirmishes through the mid game.

runes.keystoneWhy: Master-tier K'Sante players favor this over Aftershock across 18,539 games — the bonus health and proc damage reward you for landing autos during the melee trades you're forcing, which fits a lane defined by closing distance rather than tanking a burst engage.

summoners.why: Teleport is the standard pick (84.5% pick rate) for wave and map pressure in a lane where you're not forcing early kills. Flash + Ignite posts the highest measured win rate of the three combos (49.2% over a smaller sample) and matches the data's solo-kill edge if you want to commit to all-ins before level 6.

playing.title: Track the Hop cooldown
playing.detail: E (Hop) is Gnar's only real escape, on a 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s cooldown. Once he burns it to reposition or farm, that's your window to dash in with E (Footwork) and commit.

playing.title: Don't walk into the boomerang
playing.detail: Q (Boomerang Throw) reaches 1100 range and slows on hit, and catching it on the return cuts its own cooldown. Give up contested CS rather than eat free pokes while Hop is up.

playing.title: Stack Q before you commit
playing.detail: Q (Ntofo Strikes) hits a short line and grants a stack on hit; at 2 stacks it fires a shockwave that pulls Gnar in. Walk up with Q first so the pull does the gap-closing for you.

playing.title: Use W's charge to eat poke
playing.detail: W (Path Maker) takes reduced damage while charging before it dashes to knock back and stun. Hold the charge through a Q poke, then release the stun once Gnar is out of Hop range.

playing.title: All-in from level 6 when Hop is down
playing.detail: R (All Out) knocks Gnar through terrain and then transforms your kit with more damage and healing at the cost of reduced defenses. Look for this the instant his Hop is on cooldown — the solo-kill numbers are yours.

playing.title: Respect the Rage transform
playing.detail: Gnar's Rage Gene builds in combat and at max Rage transforms him into Mega Gnar, who gains his own area stun (W, Wallop) and an AoE slam on E (Crunch). Don't dump every cooldown into an extended trade right as his Rage bar nears full.

playing.title: Build into the skirmish, not around it
playing.detail: The Iceborn Gauntlet into Unending Despair into Jak'Sho path (49.6% win rate over 131 games) is built for exactly this kind of melee-vs-poke lane — it rewards you for sticking to Gnar once you've closed the gap.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, boots, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are pulled from measured K'Sante vs Gnar games on the current patch (16.19.1); the gap-control trade pattern, cooldown reads, and engage timing are my own tactical analysis.
